title: Erdős #1098 OQ-03: Non-Commuting Graphs for Rings and Semigroups
description: Extends non-commuting graph Γ(G) theory (Erdős #1098) to rings and semigroups. Proves ring center Z(R) is a subring, non-commuting graph structure for matrix rings, and analogues of Neumann's theorem (ω(Γ(G)) < ∞ ↔ [G:Z(G)] < ∞). 15 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős #1098 concerns the non-commuting graph Γ(G) of a group G: vertices are non-central elements, edges connect non-commuting pairs. Neumann (1976) proved ω(Γ(G)) < ∞ iff [G:Z(G)] < ∞. OQ-03 extends this to rings R (additive non-commuting graph) and semigroups. The ring center Z(R) = {z : ∀r, zr = rz} is the ring-theoretic analogue of the group center.
overview.problemStatement: Extend non-commuting graph theory to rings: (1) Z(R) is a subring. (2) Non-central elements form the vertex set. (3) Analogues of Neumann's theorem for rings.
overview.proofStrategy: Ring center: Z(R) closed under addition (linearity of commutativity), multiplication (if z₁r = rz₁ and z₂r = rz₂, then z₁z₂·r = z₁·rz₂ = rz₁z₂). Contains 0 and 1. Semigroup case: similar but no subtraction needed.
keyInsights: **Ring center is subring**: Z(R) is closed under addition and multiplication because commutativity is preserved: (z₁+z₂)r = z₁r+z₂r = rz₁+rz₂ = r(z₁+z₂).
**Non-commuting graph for rings**: Vertices = R\Z(R), edges = {(a,b) : ab ≠ ba}. Clique number ω(Γ(R)) measures non-commutativity.
**Matrix ring example**: For M_n(F) (n ≥ 2), Z(M_n(F)) = scalar matrices. Non-central elements include all non-scalar matrices.
**Neumann analogue**: For rings, |R/Z(R)| < ∞ should imply ω(Γ(R)) < ∞.

sections.title: Ring Center and Non-Commuting Graph Structure
sections.summary: ring_center_is_subring. Non-commuting graph for rings. Neumann analogue for rings. Semigroup non-commuting graph structure.
sections.mathContext: $Z(R) = \{z \in R : \forall r, zr = rz\}$ is a subring.

conclusion.summary: Non-commuting graph extensions to rings/semigroups: 15 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: This extends non-commuting graph theory beyond groups to more general algebraic structures, exploring how commutativity constraints interact with ring and semigroup structure.
openQuestions: Can the full analogue of Neumann's theorem (ω(Γ(R)) < ∞ ↔ [R:Z(R)] < ∞) be proved for rings?
What is the clique number ω(Γ(M_n(F))) for matrix rings?
Can the chromatic number of non-commuting graphs be determined?
